correctness.rationale: The unique eight-vertex pair is constructed by attaching four ears to an identical K4-minus-edge core. Both have degree classes of sizes (4,2,2) for degrees (2,4,5), and equitable neighbor-count matrix [[0,1,1],[2,0,2],[2,2,1]]. It is stable after degree refinement and hence C2-equivalent without depth restriction. Distinct neighborhood multiplicities among degree-two vertices prove nonisomorphism; an explicit K2,3 subgraph distinguishes the nonouterplanar graph from its outerplanar counterpart. Ear-deletion completeness and exact, hash-free isomorphism/backtracking enumerate every unlabelled 2-tree to order 8; per-order type counts (1,1,2,5,12,39) and C2-class counts (1,1,2,5,12,38) prove minimality and uniqueness. The portable verifier was executed and its output checked. OEIS A054581 independently confirms type totals. No infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The first order at which 1-WL/C2 loses graph identification within the natural maximal-treewidth-two class is a motivated sharp structural threshold. Its unique ambiguous pair at n=8 also differs in the forbidden-minor property of outerplanarity. This gives an unbounded-rank C2 nondefinability result relative to a standard graph class, a concrete expressive-power boundary beyond a mere finite count.
